sources.title: Buffer time
sources.version_or_commit: Live Support article dated 2025-03-04; current behavior may change.
sources.locator: Create a buffer time rule; FAQs about granularity, overlap, and before/after behavior.
observed_operations: web search for booking buffer rules
sources.evidence_use: Rules can vary by space; durations use platform time granularity. They affect only bookings made after implementation. If multiple conflicting rules apply to one space, the maximum is used. Rules add buffer before and after symmetrically; regular users are blocked but system users may book through; the smallest available step is 15 minutes.
sources.change_or_caveat: Symmetric setup/cleanup reservation can overblock in one-sided cases; existing bookings are not retroactively changed; admin override and plan caps require a pilot test.

sources.title: Access and Visibility

sources.title: Web Content Accessibility Guidelines 2.2
sources.version_or_commit: WCAG 2.2, W3C Recommendation 2023-10-05; normative success criteria.
sources.locator: SC 2.1.1 Keyboard; 2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum); 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value; 4.1.3 Status Messages.
observed_operations: located target-size and AT success criteria
sources.evidence_use: Keyboard operation is required for all functionality (2.1.1). Pointer targets are at least 24 by 24 CSS pixels unless an exception applies (2.5.8). UI names/roles/states/values must be exposed to assistive technology (4.1.2); status messages must be programmatically exposed without focus (4.1.3).
sources.change_or_caveat: WCAG target size is a conformance floor, not a wet-hands usability prescription. Choose larger, well-spaced controls and test with the actual tablet, screen reader, coordinator, and hands-on workflow.

sources.title: LibreBooking 7.0 administration guide
sources.version_or_commit: Documentation labels product LibreBooking 7.0.0; latest URL is mutable; source release tag v7.0.0 at commit 422b4b0223335d18c7d5f005ffcdd93719575c20 was separately checked.
sources.locator: Public Schedule Visibility and Resource Configuration.
observed_operations: read public visibility, buffer, approval, permissions, check-in/out defaults
sources.evidence_use: Unauthenticated schedule viewing is off by default; if public schedule is enabled, reservation details are still hidden by default. Resource constraints: min/max duration default to none; approval defaults off; new-user access to a resource defaults on; bookings may run up to now by default; check-in/out can be required; autorelease requires a configured job. Buffer is described as enforcing time apart, but the page does not specify unit/direction here. Administrators are exempt from usage constraints.
sources.change_or_caveat: Potentially useful self-hosted resource-calendar approach; do not promote defaults as tenant isolation. Test resource ACLs, role views, units, kiosk/public tablet exposure, and exact buffer semantics.

sources.title: LibreBooking issue, fix, regression test, and release chain for buffer item ID
sources.source_type: Project issue, merged pull request, code and release records
sources.version_or_commit: Issue #1008 opened 2026-02-14; PR #1140 merged 2026-03-13; fix commit b1394612e9e5311d0b6662cffa8e2e528667d6c3; merge commit 4bc0cf5dd17b5cbacae2fd4540800f04ea371c1e; release v4.3.0 dated 2026-04-03; current v7.0.0 code checked.
sources.locator: Issue description/closure; PR #1140 change; v4.3.0 release notes; ReservationListItem.php at v7.0.0.
observed_operations: resolved exact fix and merge commit SHAs through public GitHub REST API
sources.evidence_use: A reported infinite recursion in BufferItem::Id() could crash callers. The fix switched ID construction to the wrapped reservation item and added begin/end ID assertions. The regression test passes 3600 to WithBufferTime; the inspected test excerpt does not state the unit. The issue was closed, fix merged, and included in a release; v7 code still uses the wrapped reservation item's ID.
sources.change_or_caveat: This verifies one narrow buffer-rendering regression/fix only. It does not validate conflict rules, kitchen handoffs, or tenant-scoped access.
